chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Daqqaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Sufi narrated to us. He said: Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Habbal al-Tabari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Khashshab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Muhsin ibn Isa narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Thibyan, who said: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to a prophet from among the prophets of the Children of Israel: If you would like to meet Me tomorrow in the Guarded Sanctuary, then be in this world alone, a stranger, worried, sorrowful, and shunning the people -- like a lone bird that flies in the wastelands, eats from the tops of trees, and drinks from the water of springs. When night comes, it shelters alone and does not shelter with the other birds; it finds comfort in its Lord and shuns the other birds.

key_terms.استأنس: Finding comfort and intimacy; here, finding spiritual companionship in God alone
key_terms.حظيرة القدس: The Guarded Sanctuary (Hadhirat al-Quds), a metaphor for Paradise or the abode of divine proximity
key_terms.مستوحشا: Shunning, seeking solitude from; denotes spiritual withdrawal from worldly distractions

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about solitude and closeness to God?
ai.summary: This narration, transmitted through a chain reaching Imam al-Sadiq (AS), conveys a divine revelation to a prophet of the Children of Israel. God instructs His prophet that attaining closeness to Him in the Hereafter requires living in this world as a stranger -- detached, contemplative, and withdrawn from worldly companionship -- likened to a solitary bird that finds its comfort only in its Lord. This teaching reflects a broader Shia ascetic tradition emphasizing zuhd (worldly renunciation) as a path to divine nearness.

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. Ahmad al-Daqqaq (rh) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Harun al-Sufi narrated to us. He said: `Ubaydullah b. Musa al-Habbal al-Tabari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn al-Khashab. He said: Muhammad b. Muhsan b. `Isa from Yunus b. Thibyan. He said: Al-Sadiq (as) said:

Allah revealed to a prophet from the prophets of the Children of Israel: If you would like to meet Me anon in the Guarded Sanctuary, then be, in this world, alone, strange, worried, sorrowful, and away from the people – like a bird flying by itself in an uninhabited land, eating from the tops of trees, and drinking from the water of rivers. When night comes, it dwells alone, without seeking refuge in the other birds, and it finds comfort in its Lord away from the birds.
